title: Staged dry-run simulation framework and rollback choreography for Optimize auto-tuner regressions
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: After a recent Optimize auto-tuner rollout that reduced per-token cost aggressively for a subset of workloads, we observed a correlated increase in tail latency and a small but measurable uptick in error rates for long-context generation jobs. This ticket scopes building a deterministic dry-run simulation harness and a surgical rollback choreography so future tuning changes can be validated safely and reverted with minimal blast radius.

Background: The auto-tuner applied a new batching/cache policy permutation across the hosted fleet (canary -> staged). During canary we saw minimal regressions, but a workload distribution shift in production caused batch coalescing heuristics to over-aggregate long-sequence requests, increasing p95/p99 latency and causing downstream caller timeouts. Existing safeguards detected the problem but rollback took longer than desired because the applied changes spanned multiple layers (executor kernels, prefix-caching policies, and routing weights).

Goal: Deliver three things: (1) a dry-run simulation framework that replays production traces against proposed tuner configs and emits cost/latency/regression risk fingerprints; (2) a canonical rollback choreography that can revert a staged apply across runtime, routing, and cache layers in a single orchestrated operation; (3) an incident-playbook document for on-call and SRE with automated run commands and clear escalation rules.
postmortem_summary:
Root cause: aggressive coalescing threshold in the new batching profile coupled with a change in sequence-length distribution for a tenant class. Contributing factors: insufficient synthetic coverage for long-tail workloads in canary, and no single-step revert that touched routing weights, executor feature flags, and cache warmup profiles. Detection: automated SLO monitors detected p99 latency increase (+42%) and error rate (+0.9%) within 12 minutes of rollout. Recovery: manual multi-step rollback restored baseline after 48 minutes.

Impact: Medium (intermittent end-user timeouts for several customers with long-context generation; transient errors for internal CI and downstream pipelines). Costs: short-term cost decreased due to higher batching but offset by retries/reprovisioning. Learnings: need faster validation, played-back traces, and atomic revert ability across layers.

reproduction_steps: 1) Pull production trace sample for tenant group 'longgen' from trace-store (query: service:inference AND tag:tenant=longgen range:2026-03-02T10:00:00Z..2026-03-02T11:00:00Z)
2) Run trace through local simulator with proposed tuner config (flag: --dryrun-simulate-batching) and record per-request latency and batch size distribution
3) Compare dry-run fingerprint vs baseline: p50/p95/p99 latency, error markers, and batch coalescing events
4) If p99 delta > 20% or error rate delta > 0.5% mark as high-risk and fail automated apply
5) To reproduce the rollback path, apply the staging change then execute the rollback choreography script with --simulate to validate idempotency
proposed_design:
Dry-run simulator: a replay engine that consumes sampled traces and applies the exact order of requests to a sandboxed runtime image. The simulator will: (a) emulate routing and queuing delays, (b) replicate batch coalescing heuristics deterministically, (c) model cache warm/warmup penalties by ingesting KV snapshots. Outputs: a deterministic fingerprint (compact vector) with: cost delta, p50/p95/p99 latency deltas, error-rate delta, batch-size histogram delta.

Rollback choreography: a single orchestration step that sequences three idempotent primitives: 1) set routing weight back to previous commit via control-plane API, 2) toggle executor feature flags using staged config sets (supports dry-run preview), 3) restore cache warmup profile and optionally trigger cache-priming job. All steps must have a consistent canary-id and be reversible via the same orchestration routine.
playbook_steps: Detect: Automated SLO alert for p99 latency or error-rate delta > thresholds triggers incident channel and runs preliminary triage script (scripts/triage/collect_optimize_facts.sh).
Triage: Run dry-run simulator on latest traces (tools/optimize-sim --trace-id=<id> --config=<candidate>) to decide if change should be reverted immediately.
Mitigate: If simulator indicates high risk, execute routing-weight clamp (rctl set-weight --canary-id=<id> --weight=0.01).
Revert: Execute rollback choreography (tools/rollback-optimize --canary-id=<id> --mode=orchestrated) which performs weight restore, executor-flag revert, and cache-profile restore in that order.
Validate: After rollback, run smoke-suite (internal/regression/smoke.sh) and replay a small sample through the simulator to ensure fingerprint matches pre-change baseline.
Post-incident: Attach traces, simulator fingerprints, and cache snapshots to the incident ticket and schedule a 1-week follow-up to implement preventive controls.
automation_requirements: A reproducible trace-sampling pipeline that exports anonymized request sequences to GCS daily
A sandboxed runtime image that matches production kernels and kv-cache semantics for deterministic replay
A control-plane API to perform atomic routing-weight updates with canary-id metadata
Instrumentation hooks to snapshot batch composition and cache state at canary boundaries

testing_plan: Unit: add deterministic unit tests for batch coalescing heuristics and cache warmup emulator. Integration: run nightly replay jobs against master with historical traces and assert fingerprint invariants. Canary: require dry-run simulator pass for 2 consecutive canary increments before routing weight increase. Chaos: schedule a controlled chaos window where rollback choreography is exercised against synthetic regressions.
rollback_choreography: Step 0: Abort new applies (if active) and mark canary-id as 'rollback-in-progress'
Step 1: Reduce routing weight to 1% using control-plane with synchronous confirmation
Step 2: Toggle executor feature flags to previous commit using staged config API and wait for health-checks
Step 3: Restore cache warmup/profile; if partial cache corruption suspected, trigger cache-prime job for affected shards
Step 4: Run validation replay on a 1% production trace sample and confirm p99 within threshold
Step 5: If validation fails, escalate to SRE lead and initiate broader traffic diversion while engineering investigates
